literal: The prognostication states: "The heir apparent will be anxious."
idiomatic: The gloss warns of peril to the crown prince.

literal: At this time the crown prince constantly had severe illness.
idiomatic: The heir was chronically and gravely ill.

literal: In the seventeenth year, seventh month, day Dingchou, the Great White was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: Seventeenth year, seventh month, dingchou: Venus by day.

literal: On day Dingyou in the tenth month, it again was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: Tenth month, dingyou: another daylight Venus.

literal: In the sixth month of the eighteenth year, it again was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: Eighteenth year, sixth month: Venus again shone by day.

literal: In the fifth month of the nineteenth year, it again was seen in daytime in the Willow.
idiomatic: Nineteenth year, May: daylight Venus in the Willow.

literal: On day Xinyou in the sixth month, it again was seen in daytime in the Ghost Cart.
idiomatic: June, xinyou: daylight Venus in the Ghost asterism.

literal: In the ninth month, it again was seen in the Chariot.
idiomatic: September: Venus reappeared in the Chariot.

literal: In the sixth month of the twentieth year, Mars entered the Celestial Granary.
idiomatic: Twentieth year, sixth month: Mars entered the Celestial Granary (Heaven’s round-silo asterism).

literal: The prognostication states: "Great famine."
idiomatic: The omen reads: widespread starvation.

literal: On day Dinghai in the seventh month, the Great White was seen in daytime, in the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: July, dinghai: Venus blazed by day inside the Supreme Palace.

literal: The prognostication states: "When the Great White enters the Supreme Palace Enclosure, the state will have grief."
idiomatic: Venus inside the enclosure spells national mourning.

literal: Being seen in daytime means arms and mourning.
idiomatic: Daylight appearance adds war and funerals.

literal: In the twelfth month, day Jisi, the moon transgressed the Gate-bolt and the eastern and western Sincerity stars.
idiomatic: December, jisi: the Moon crossed the Gate-bolt and the east and west Sincerity stars.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Gate-bolt governs heart, belly, throat, and tongue; the eastern and western Sincerity govern secret plots."
idiomatic: The bolt-stars watch intimates and spokesmen; the Sincerity pair marks hidden intrigue.

literal: On day Renshen in the second month of the twenty-first year, the Great White was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: Twenty-first year, second month, renshen: Venus by day.

literal: On day Guimao in the third month, the Great White continuously was seen in daytime, in the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: March, guimao: Venus lingered visible by day in the Feathered Forest.

literal: The prognostication states: "There will be a strong minister; there will be arms and mourning; central-army troops will rise."
idiomatic: Foretells a domineering minister, battle and bereavement, and palace-army upheaval.

literal: In the third month, the Great White was seen in daytime in the Stomach.
idiomatic: March: daylight Venus in the Stomach lodge.

literal: The prognostication states: "Central-army troops will rise."
idiomatic: Household guards mobilize.

literal: On day Renwu in the fourth month, the Great White entered the Celestial Granary.
idiomatic: April, renwu: Venus entered the Celestial Granary.

literal: The prognostication states: "There will be famine."
idiomatic: Portends hunger.

literal: In the sixth month, Jupiter transgressed the Weeping star.
idiomatic: June: Jupiter crossed the Weeping star.

literal: The prognostication states: "There will be weeping affairs."
idiomatic: Mourning follows.

literal: In that year’s ninth month, the emperor died.
idiomatic: That September the sovereign died.

literal: In the first Long’an year, Wang Gong and others raised troops to coerce the court; thereupon inner and outer were placed on alert, and Wang Guobao was killed to appease them.
idiomatic: Long’an one: Wang Gong’s coalition menaced Jiankang; the capital locked down and Wang Guobao was executed as a sop.

literal: Moreover, successive years of flood and drought stirred the three fronts and the masses starved.
idiomatic: Years of weather disaster roiled three war zones while commoners went hungry.

literal: In Emperor An’s first Long’an year, first month, day Guihai, Mars transgressed the Weeping star.
idiomatic: Long’an one, first month, guihai: Mars crossed the Weeping star.

literal: The prognostication states: "There will be weeping affairs."
idiomatic: Again: royal mourning.

literal: On day Dingchou in the fourth month, the Great White was seen in daytime, in the Eastern Well.
idiomatic: April, dingchou: Venus by day in the Eastern Well.

literal: The prognostication states: "Qin will have arms and mourning."
idiomatic: The northwestern Qin theater faces war and death.

literal: In the sixth month, Yao Xing attacked Luoyang; Xi Hui sent troops to rescue it.
idiomatic: June: Yao Xing struck Luoyang while Xi Hui dispatched relief.

literal: In winter Yao Chang died; his son Lie succeeded him.
idiomatic: Winter: Yao Chang died and his son Yao Xing (Lie) took the throne.

literal: The Prince of Wei, Gui, assumed position at Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Wei prince Tuoba Gui mounted the throne at Zhongshan.

literal: That eighth month, Mars guarded the Well’s battle-axe stars.
idiomatic: That August Mars stationed at the Eastern Well’s axe stars.

literal: The prognostication states: "Great ministers will be executed."
idiomatic: Senior officials face execution.

literal: In the second year, sixth month, day Wuchen, Sheti moved across degrees abnormally.
idiomatic: Second year, sixth month, wuchen: the Sheti pointer jumped its proper step.

literal: Jupiter was seen in daytime, in the Stomach, the field allotment of Yan Province.
idiomatic: Jupiter shone by day in the Stomach, Yanzhou’s celestial field.

literal: In that year’s sixth month, Xi Hui sent Zheng Qifang and others with ten thousand men to attack Murong Bao at Huatai; they were defeated and returned.
idiomatic: That June Xi Hui sent Zheng Qifang’s ten-thousand-man column against Murong Bao at Huatai; it retreated in defeat.

literal: In the intercalary month, the Great White was seen in daytime, in the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: Leap month: daylight Venus in the Feathered Forest.

literal: On day Dingchou, the moon transgressed the eastern upper minister.
idiomatic: Dingchou: the Moon crossed the eastern upper minister star.

literal: In the third year, fifth month, day Xinyou, the moon again covered the eastern upper minister.
idiomatic: Third year, May, xinyou: the Moon again occulted the eastern upper minister.

literal: On day Xinwei, Mercury transgressed the great star of the Coachman.
idiomatic: Xinwei: Mercury crossed Xuanyuan’s chief star.

literal: The prognostications were all the same as above.
idiomatic: The glosses matched prior entries.

literal: In the second year’s ninth month, Yu Kai and others raised troops, memorializing to execute Wang Yu and others; thereupon inner and outer were placed on alert.
idiomatic: Second year, September: Yu Kai’s faction mobilized to demand Wang Yu’s head; the realm went on war footing.

literal: In the third year’s sixth month, Luoyang fell to bandits.
idiomatic: Third year, June: Luoyang was lost to raiders.

literal: Huan Xuan broke Jing Province; Yong Province killed Yin Zhongkan and others.
idiomatic: Huan Xuan shattered Jingzhou while Yongzhou forces slew Yin Zhongkan and his circle.

literal: Sun En gathered a host, attacked and took Kuaiji, and killed the interior governor.
idiomatic: Sun En’s rebels seized Kuaiji and executed the governor.

literal: In the fourth year, sixth month, day Xinyou, the moon transgressed the Weeping star.
idiomatic: Fourth year, June, xinyou: the Moon crossed the Weeping star.

literal: In the fifth year, first month, the Great White was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: Fifth year, first month: Venus by day.

literal: From the previous year’s twelfth month it had been seen in daytime in the Dipper until this month’s Yimao day.
idiomatic: Since the prior twelfth month Venus had stayed visible by day in the Dipper until yimao of this month.

literal: Investigating the prognostication: "The calamity lies in Wu and Yue."
idiomatic: Commentary places the omen in the Wu-Yue southeast.

literal: On day Guihai in the seventh month, the Great Horn star scattered, trembled, and showed five colors.
idiomatic: July, guihai: Arcturus flickered in polychrome bursts.

literal: The prognostication states: "The king will be scattered and dispersed."
idiomatic: Portends a sovereign driven from his throne.

literal: On day Dingmao, the moon transgressed the Celestial Pass.
idiomatic: Dingmao: the Moon crossed the Celestial Pass.

literal: The prognostication states: "The king will be anxious."
idiomatic: Royal worry is foretold.

literal: On day Gengzi in the ninth month, Mars transgressed Shao Wei and then guarded it.
idiomatic: September, gengzi: Mars crossed Shao Wei and stationed there.

literal: The prognostication states: "Recluses will be executed."
idiomatic: Hermit-scholars face the headsman.

literal: On day Jiazi in the tenth month, the moon transgressed the eastern secondary minister.
idiomatic: October, jiazi: the Moon crossed the eastern secondary minister.

literal: In that year’s seventh month, Grand Empress Dowager Li died.
idiomatic: That July Grand Empress Dowager Li passed away.

literal: In the tenth month, occult bandits greatly defeated Gao Yazhi at Yuyao; seven or eight tenths died.
idiomatic: October: rebel sorcerers shattered Gao Yazhi at Yuyao with seventy to eighty percent losses.

literal: In the fifth year, Sun En attacked counties, killed interior governors, reached Jingkou, advanced to Pu Islet, and thereupon inner and outer were placed on alert.
idiomatic: Fifth year: Sun En raided commanderies, slew governors, pushed to Jingkou and Pu Islet, and put the capital region on alert.

literal: En sent a separate general to attack Guangling, killing more than three thousand; he withdrew to hold Yuzhou, at which time Liu Yu again pursued and broke him.
idiomatic: Sun En’s column hit Guangling, killed three thousand-plus, then fell back to Yuzhou island until Liu Yu chased and crushed them.

literal: In the ninth month, Huan Xuan’s memorial arrived, defying the decree and lording over the sovereign.
idiomatic: September: Huan Xuan’s arrogant memorial snubbed the throne.

literal: In the tenth month, Sima Yuanxian greatly drilled a river army intending to attack Xuan.
idiomatic: October: Sima Yuanxian mass-trained a fleet to strike Huan Xuan.

literal: In the first month of the first Yuanxing year, Lu Xun styled himself General Who Subdues Caitiffs, led the remainder of Sun En’s host, and seized ground in Yongjia and Jin’an.
idiomatic: Yuanxing one, first month: Lu Xun claimed the caitiff-subduing generalship, inherited Sun En’s bands, and carved out Yongjia and Jin’an.

literal: In the second month, the emperor in battle dress dispatched the western army.
idiomatic: February: the emperor, in armor, sent the western host.

literal: In the third month, Huan Xuan took the capital, killed Sima Yuanxian, and banished Grand Tutor and Prince of Kuaiji, Daozi.
idiomatic: March: Huan Xuan seized Jiankang, executed Sima Yuanxian, and exiled Prince Daozi of Kuaiji.

literal: In Yuanxing first year, third month, day Wuzi, the Great White transgressed the Five Feudal Lords and thereby was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: Yuanxing one, third month, wuzi: Venus crossed the Five Feudal Lords and shone by day.

literal: The prognostication states: "Feudal lords will be executed."
idiomatic: Regional lords face execution.

literal: On day Wuyin in the seventh month, Mars was in the Eastern Well.
idiomatic: July, wuyin: Mars stood in the Eastern Well.

literal: Mars transgressed the Ghost Cart and Heap of Corpses.
idiomatic: Mars crossed the Ghost asterism and the corpse-pile stars.

literal: The prognostications were all the same as above.
idiomatic: Glosses repeated earlier lines.

literal: On day Bingyin in the eighth month, the Great White covered the right Law Enforcer.
idiomatic: August, bingyin: Venus occulted the right Law Enforcer.

literal: On day Guiwei in the ninth month, the Great White transgressed Advancing Worthy.
idiomatic: September, guiwei: Venus crossed the Advancing Worthy star.

literal: The prognostication states: "Those of Advancing Worthy will be executed."
idiomatic: Men tied to the Advancing Worthy star face death.

literal: In the second year, second month, Jupiter transgressed the western upper general.
idiomatic: Second year, February: Jupiter crossed the western upper general.

literal: On day Jiachen in the sixth month, the moon covered the fourth star of the Dipper.
idiomatic: June, jiachen: the Moon occulted the Dipper’s fourth star.

literal: The prognostication states: "Great ministers will be executed; within three years."
idiomatic: High ministers die, within three years’ span.

literal: On day Guichou in the eighth month, the Great White transgressed the second northern star of the Chamber.
idiomatic: August, guichou: Venus crossed the Chamber’s second north star.

literal: On day Jichou in the ninth month, Jupiter transgressed Advancing Worthy, and Mars transgressed the western upper general.
idiomatic: September, jichou: Jupiter crossed Advancing Worthy while Mars crossed the western upper general.

literal: On day Jiaxu in the tenth month, the Great White transgressed the Weeping star.
idiomatic: October, jiaxu: Venus crossed the Weeping star.

literal: On day Dingyou in the eleventh month, Mars transgressed the eastern upper minister.
idiomatic: November, dingyou: Mars crossed the eastern upper minister.

literal: On day Yisi in the twelfth month, the moon covered the second star of the Coachman.
idiomatic: December, yisi: the Moon occulted Xuanyuan’s second star.

literal: The prognostications were all the same as above.
idiomatic: Omen glosses matched prior citations.

literal: In the first year’s winter, Wei broke Yao Xing’s army.
idiomatic: First year winter: Northern Wei shattered Yao Xing’s host.

literal: In the twelfth month of the second year, Huan Xuan usurped the throne, banished emperor and empress to Xunyang, and made Empress He of Yong’an the Lady of Lingling.
idiomatic: Second year, twelfth month: Huan Xuan seized the throne, exiled the sovereigns to Xunyang, and demoted Empress He to Lady of Lingling.

literal: In the third year’s second month, Liu Yu exterminated the entire Huan clan.
idiomatic: Third year, February: Liu Yu wiped out the Huans.

literal: In the third year, first month, day Wuxu, Mars retrograded and transgressed the western upper minister of the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: Third year, first month, wuxu: Mars moved retrograde against the enclosure’s western upper minister.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Son of Heaven battles in the field; the upper minister dies."
idiomatic: Portends a ruler fighting in the open and a chief minister’s death.

literal: On day Bingchen in the second month, Mars retrograded, northwest of the Left Law Enforcer.
idiomatic: February, bingchen: Mars hung retrograde northwest of the Left Law Enforcer.

literal: The prognostication states: "Law enforcers will be executed."
idiomatic: Judicial stars mark executions.

literal: On day Jiawu in the fourth month, the moon covered the second star of the Coachman.
idiomatic: April, jiawu: the Moon occulted Xuanyuan’s second star.

literal: On day Renshen in the fifth month, the moon covered the second star of the Dipper, and Saturn entered the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: May, renshen: the Moon occulted the Dipper’s second star while Saturn entered the Feathered Forest.

literal: The prognostications were all the same as above.
idiomatic: Glosses again matched earlier ones.

literal: In that year’s second month, on day Bingchen, Liu Yu killed Huan Xiu and others.
idiomatic: That February, bingchen, Liu Yu slew Huan Xiu and associates.

literal: In the third month, on day Jiwei, he routed Huan Xuan and sent armies west to pursue him.
idiomatic: March, jiwei: Liu Yu broke Huan Xuan and launched western pursuit columns.

literal: On day Xinsi, he executed Left Director Wang Yu; Huan Xuan seized the Son of Heaven and went to Jiangling.
idiomatic: Xinsi: Wang Yu the left director was beheaded while Huan Xuan abducted the emperor toward Jiangling.

literal: In the fifth month, Xuan came down to Zhengrong Islet and the righteous army destroyed him.
idiomatic: May: Huan Xuan descended to Zhengrong Islet where the loyalist host annihilated him.

literal: Huan Zhen again attacked and took Jiangling, imprisoned and coerced the Son of Heaven.
idiomatic: Huan Zhen retook Jiangling, holding the emperor captive.
